caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The chart is a grouped horizontal bar chart displaying negative log probabilities for clinically relevant tokens across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, which are labeled along the x-axis in that order. The y-axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at intervals of 1 unit. Each specialty group contains seven bars: one light blue bar representing the baseline Mistralv0.2-Base model, and six colored bars (light peach to dark brown) representing the model fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, as indicated in the legend. The legend specifies the color coding: Cardio (light peach), Gastro (peach), Infect (light orange), Neuro (orange), Obstetrics (dark orange), and Pediatrics (dark brown). Within each group, the baseline (light blue) bar is consistently the tallest, indicating the highest negative log probability (weakest prediction), while the fine-tuned bars are shorter, indicating improved performance. For example, in the Cardio group, the baseline bar reaches approximately -22.5, while the fine-tuned bars range from about -23.5 to -26.5, with the Pediatrics-fine-tuned bar being the shortest. Similarly, in the Infect group, the baseline bar is at approximately -23.5, and the fine-tuned bars range from about -24 to -25.5. The Gastro-fine-tuned model consistently shows the lowest negative log probability (shortest bars) across most specialty groups, suggesting strong generalization. The bars are arranged in groups by specialty, with no sorting by value, and no visual emphasis such as shading or annotation is applied to any bar.
